added_failures_note: not derivable from gate arms: the reviewed manifest records baseline_suite null and after_suite null, so neither arm exists to diff and no failure id can be attributed. The reviewed node is an evidence node whose gate was a script rerun, recorded at rescore.log with EXIT=0 and rows_match=True.

findings.text: follow-on: probe.log's worker line reads 'cost=0.000309 running=0.000309 category=core_plasma', but run.py:302 prints only '{ids:32s} cost={cost:.6f}' and no 'running=' or 'category=' field occurs anywhere in the committed script, so that log's body came from an earlier revision while its header, rewritten after the run, names the committed command. The declared control for this node is the equilibrium probe, so the one log carrying it does not reconcile with the artefact it is offered as evidence for.

follow-on: build_state feeds the IDS's stored_path_domain_mix into the state, and the plan records the DD path classification is degenerate (61,337 of 61,366 DD nodes carry exactly their IDS's domain), so the mix re-supplies the current mapped domain the brief deliberately withheld; measured on the landed results, 59 of 87 rows have the current domain as their top path-mix domain and 50 of the 53 confirms_current rows do, so those confirmations cannot be read as independent of the current map (6 rows went against the mix, so it is a bias rather than a dictator).

follow-on: rescore() compares recomputed rows against payload['rows'] using the same build_rows that produced them, so the assertion moves with the code under test: it reddens if build_rows is edited later and stays green if build_rows was wrong when the rows were stored, which is the regression a durability claim would have to rest on.

follow-on: write_fragment hardcodes '87 IDSs scored' in the fragment prose while every other figure in it is interpolated from the payload, so a rerun over a different IDS set would emit a fragment contradicting its own inputs, and --rescore does not regenerate the fragment to catch it.

follow-on: score_one re-implements the two-level tree composition that decide_domain_tree at imas_codex/graph/dd_domain_classifier.py:1086 already owns, duplicating the per-category probability lookup and the category*dimension product rather than extending the owner, whose entry point is path-shaped and cannot carry this IDS-level state; decide_domain_tree has no caller in imas_codex/, so one state-driven core would serve both.

follow-on: the fragment presents its 21/53/10/3 classification and 33 changed map rows as three tables and no figure, although the declared write paths reserve docs/figures/sn-catalog-grouping/scg-ids-map-jev and the project's figure mandate asks for a graphic wherever one would aid understanding.
